CyanogenMod 12.1 Snapshots With AOSP's November Security Updates Now Hitting Devices

I have a question about cyanogen for any of the more experienced folks out there. How do I update it? Am I just supposed to reflash it with a newer version every couple months, or can I do it internally?

Great question! You can download the full nightly (or stable) version and reflash it manually from recovery, or use the built-in updater located in Settings>About>CyanogenMod Updates, but what you're probably interested in is called "delta updates", which is the ability to download only the update data that's changed. Typically we're talking less than 30MB per nightly. I don't believe CyanogenMod has delta updating built-in, but you can use a delta updater app to provide this feature.

The delta updater will ask you to provide your current ".zip" file (the full nightly or stable version) and keep it in a specific folder. Then whenever an update is available, the delta updater will give you the option to download only the changed data, which it will then merge with your existing stored ".zip" file in order to create an exact copy of the most current ".zip". You can flash this .zip file manually with your recovery software, or if you have a supported recovery (typically TWRP or CMW-based Recovery) the app can queue up the .zip file automatically and reboot into recovery to apply the update for you. You can also tell your delta updater to flash an additional .zip after each nightly build, which I use to reflash my SuperSU.zip package after each delta update.

I use CyanDelta as my delta updater, although CM Downloader is a good one as well. Note that you need root access for the auto-apply functionality, otherwise you can download the delta updates and manually flash through your preferred recovery.
